Forecast Discussion

High pressure is over the central Appalachians through Friday. The air is very dry, winds are light, and skies are sunny. Nights are cold in valleys, and afternoons warm nicely.

An upper-level disturbance over the eastern Gulf of Mexico moves slowly east. It spreads high clouds over us Friday.

Saturday, that disturbance forms low pressure off the Florida coast as our high moves to New England. An easterly flow between the two brings thicker clouds and a cooler afternoon. I cannot rule out rain Saturday afternoon and evening.

The low strengthens as it moves north along the Carolina coast Sunday. Periods of light rain fall here Sunday, with more near the Blue Ridge and less near the Tennessee line. We are on the western fringe of the rain. How close the low tracks to the coast decides how much rain falls. That part remains uncertain.

A front arrives from the west Sunday night with showers possible. Monday is breezy and cooler.

Colder air arrives Tuesday with a shower possible. Showers are more likely Wednesday as a chilly wedge develops down the east side of the Appalachians. Maybe we can sneak in a dry but cool Thanksgiving Day.
